question: What is the primary site of lymphatic drainage for vulval tumours?
explanation: The external genitalia drain primarily to the superficial and deep inguinal lymph nodes, making node assessment critical in staging. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why do patients frequently experience a delayed diagnosis when developing a vulval growth?

options.A: Social stigma and misattribution to common skin conditions
options.B: Symptoms mimic common urinary tract infections exclusively
options.C: Complete absence of any visible or palpable changes
options.D: Rapid metastatic spread hides the primary vulval lesion

explanation: Patients often mistake early vulval lesions for hemorrhoids, yeast infections, or chafing, delaying professional medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which histological type represents the vast majority of malignant vulval tumours?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma arises from the stratified squamous epithelium of the vulva and makes up the vast majority of malignant diagnoses. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h2)

question: What fundamental characteristic separates a benign vulval cyst from a malignant vulval tumour?

options.A: Malignant tumours exclusively affect postmenopausal women
options.B: Benign lesions cause intense pruritus while malignant ones are always pain-free
options.C: Benign growths remain localized without invading adjacent tissues or spreading
options.D: Benign cysts require immediate radical surgical excision

explanation: The defining feature of benign masses is their localized nature, lacking the tissue invasion and metastatic potential seen in malignancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which chronic dermatological condition is a well-known precursor to non-HPV-related vulval squamous cell carcinoma?
explanation: Long-standing lichen sclerosus causes structural changes and chronic inflammation of the vulval skin, increasing the risk of malignant transformation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h3)

question: How does the pathogenesis of HPV-related vulval cancer typically differ from non-HPV-related cases?

options.A: Non-HPV-related tumours respond best to antiviral medications
options.B: HPV-related tumours never originate from squamous cells
options.C: Non-HPV-related tumours are primarily driven by chronic inflammatory skin diseases
options.D: HPV-related tumours occur exclusively in geriatric populations

explanation: While HPV-related cancers are linked to viral integration in younger women, non-HPV pathways are driven by chronic inflammatory states like lichen sclerosus in older women. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the single most common symptom reported by patients with early vulval malignancy?
explanation: Chronic, unremitting itching of the vulva that fails to respond to standard anti-fungal or anti-inflammatory treatments is the hallmark presenting complaint. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h4)

question: A patient presents with a chronic vulval ulcer that has hard, rolled edges and does not heal. What clinical suspicion should this raise?
explanation: Non-healing ulcers with indurated, raised margins are highly suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma and warrant urgent biopsy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the mandatory diagnostic procedure to confirm a suspected vulval malignancy?
explanation: Histological confirmation via biopsy is essential because clinical appearance alone cannot reliably distinguish between benign, pre-malignant, and malignant lesions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: Why is assessing the depth of invasion crucial in the pathology report of a vulval biopsy?

options.A: It guides surgical staging and treatment planning
options.B: It eliminates the need for physical examination of the groin
options.C: It proves whether the patient used topical steroids
options.D: It determines whether the patient has an active viral infection

explanation: The depth of invasion directly influences whether a wide local excision is sufficient or if more extensive nodal surgery and adjuvant therapies are required. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary surgical goal when performing a wide local excision for an early vulval tumour?

options.A: Complete removal of the uterus and ovaries
options.B: Achieving clear histological margins around the lesion
options.C: Total ablation of the clitoral structure
options.D: Preservation of the inguinal lymph nodes only

explanation: The primary objective is to excise the tumour entirely while preserving as much normal anatomy as possible, ensuring no cancer cells remain at the edges. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h6)

question: What is the clinical advantage of performing a sentinel lymph node biopsy over a complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in early-stage vulval cancer?

options.A: It eliminates the need for general anesthesia
options.B: It completely cures systemic metastatic disease
options.C: It minimizes surgical morbidity such as lower limb lymphedema
options.D: It replaces the need for a primary tumour biopsy

explanation: Sampling only the sentinel node spares the patient from the extensive removal of all groin nodes, significantly reducing postoperative complications like chronic lymphedema and wound breakdown. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is an indwelling urinary catheter frequently managed in the immediate postoperative period following radical vulval surgery?

options.A: To eliminate the need for intravenous fluid administration
options.B: To treat underlying chronic urinary tract infections
options.C: To prevent urine contamination of the surgical wound
options.D: To measure precise glomerular filtration rates

explanation: Diverting urine away from the fresh perineal and vulval incisions protects the vulnerable suture lines from chemical irritation and bacterial contamination. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h7)

question: A patient who underwent a radical vulvectomy expresses profound distress regarding her body image and future intimate relationships. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Reassure her that physical appearance does not matter after surviving cancer
options.B: Focus strictly on physical wound care and avoid discussing emotional topics
options.C: Provide a supportive space for her to share feelings and offer referral for counseling
options.D: Advise her to ignore sexual concerns until wound healing is entirely finished

explanation: Holistic nursing care requires addressing the psychological and psychosexual impact of altering sensitive anatomical structures, validating patient grief and facilitating professional support. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h7)

question: Which factor has the most significant influence on the overall prognosis of a patient with vulval cancer?

options.C: Type of soap used for hygiene
options.D: Patient age at the time of diagnosis

explanation: Regional lymph node involvement is the single most critical prognostic indicator for survival in vulval malignancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h8)

question: What is a common long-term physical complication for patients who undergo an inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy?
explanation: Disruption or removal of the groin lymphatic channels impairs fluid drainage from the legs, frequently resulting in long-term swelling and discomfort. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h8)
